reader.requirement: At 1985 every argument-1 of FUNCTION MEAN must be class numeric (an arithmetic expression, §1989:A.2.2 type 1), so the compiler must refuse alphabetic, alphanumeric, nonnumeric-literal, group, numeric-edited and alphanumeric-function arguments and accept numeric items, literals, expressions, nested numeric functions and ALL-subscripted numeric tables.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 window: IntroducedIn 85 against DialectLevel; MEAN available at 85 and 2023

reader.notes: The Verified row Uniform('n') screens every position through Admissible('n') = class numeric; numeric-edited is projected as class alphanumeric and refused, as 1985 classes it. Diagnostics cite 2023 clauses at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: Probe src/allrmstat.cob at --std 85 (runs/allrmstat-001): COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MEAN (N-EL (ALL) (1:1)) over PIC 9(2) elements 11 72 33 compiles and prints MEAN[0003.6666] = (1+7+3)/3: each argument is a reference-modified numeric item, class alphanumeric by §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5 applied per element by GR3a, so §1989:A.2.24.3 AR1 ('Argument-1 must be class numeric') requires a refusal; the compiler decodes the digits instead. Same at --std 2023 (runs/allrmstat-002). Control: the non-ALL form MEAN (N-ITEM (1:2) 5) IS refused with COBOL1627 (src/rmstat.cob runs/rmstat-001), so the screen misses only the ALL+ref-mod shape. cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.24.3 AR1  (2.24.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3a ...'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5 ...'.
